newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil hopeful it will auction CVRD on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil hopeful it will auction CVRD on Tuesday.

text.p: Brazil was close to overcoming the last hurdles blocking the sale of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce and officials said they were cautiously optimistic the auction would take place on Tuesday.
Just two injunctions in Rio de Janeiro courts remained blocking the CVRD auction after the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) threw out 27 court cases against the privatization late on Monday evening.
The STJ decision was the government's biggest victory since the CVRD sale -- originally scheduled for April 29 -- was suspended due to a flurry of court actions across the country.
"I don't want to guarantee any date, because there are still a few obstacles that need to be resolved between today and tomorrow," Planning Minister Antonio Kandir told reporters on Monday evening.

The decision to carry out the CVRD auction on Tuesday will depend on the ability of the National Development Bank (BNDES) lawyers to successfully appeal the two injunctions currently before the Rio de Janeiro courts.
"Tomorrow perhaps we will have good news," said Jose Pio Borges, the BNDES privatization director.

Newspapers said the BNDES were so enthused by the STJ's favorable ruling late Monday, it went so far as to warn the two consortia bidding for CVRD to remain on hold in case it decided to go ahead with the auction last night.
Analysts were generally optimistic the government had finally overcome the main obstacles in the way of the CVRD auction after two weeks of intense legal wrangling.
"Sale of CVRD may go ahead today after court rejects block of legal attempt to halt auction," Bozano Simonsen investment bank told clients in its morning newsletter.
The delays surrounding the CVRD privatization appear to have benefitted some while irritating others.

Newspapers said Benjamin Steinbruch, chairman of Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN), a Brazilian steelmill which is leading one of the two groups that will be bidding for CVRD, had used the additional time to reorganize his team and convince possible defectors to remain in his consortia.

Meanwhile Votorantim president, Antonio Ermirio de Moraes, whose consortia is widely-considered the favorite to carry the CVRD auction, told reporters he was beginning to become irritated by the delays.
"It's a very unpleasant situation," Moraes told reporters adding that Brazil was putting on a spectacle of "Third World" unprofessionalism.
Newspapers said the bidding consortia were not alone is suffering a loss as a result of the delays in the auction.
The BNDES has reportedly logged up additional lawyers fees of at least $280,000 in the last couple of weeks as a result of the flood of injunctions aimed at blocking the sale.
